span: The statute forbids taking of cognizance by the court against a public servant except with the previous sanction of an authority competent to grant such sanction
why: Quoted paragraph of Nanjappa on the importance of s.19 sanction; the court notes the earlier case was referred to with approval but does not itself restate this paragraph as its holding.

span: In such situations, there is no necessity for obtaining sanction.
why: State's counsel argues that where no authority can grant sanction none is needed; a party submission, not the court's view.

span: The accused public servant does not have a right to be afforded a chance to explain the alleged disproportionate assets to the investigating officer before the filing of a chargesheet
why: Headnote on disproportionate-assets procedure and framing of charge; not about sanction.

span: It is not every offence committed by a public servant that requires sanction for prosecution under Section 197(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure
why: Quoted Amrik Singh test: sanction is needed only where the act is directly connected with official duty; adoption by the present court is not stated in this passage.

span: Words and phrases used in s. 19(1) of the P.C Act itself make it evident that the provision is mandatory in nature
why: Headnote holding: s.19 sanction is mandatory before taking cognizance of PC Act offences against a public servant, even on a s.319 CrPC application.
